scope: UI and internet aesthetics relevant to 2000–2026, with earlier roots and contemporary revivals distinguished

sources.title: CARI project history
sources.supports: Research history and original versus revival terminology; aesthetic emergence differs from when researchers named it.

sources.title: CARI: Y2K Aesthetic
sources.supports: Millennium futurist motifs; period metadata is inconsistent with CARI's history, so exact origin bounds are not copied.

sources.title: CARI: Neo-Y2K
sources.supports: A revival with saturated graphics and convergence with Metalheart, not an interchangeable name for original Y2K.

sources.title: CARI: Metalheart
sources.supports: Abstract millennium-era digital forms and the Metalheart book/creator lineage.

sources.title: CARI: Vectorheart
sources.supports: Futuristic vector forms with Swiss/utilitarian typographic influences.

sources.title: CARI: Neo-Vectorheart
sources.supports: Later revival combining angular Vectorheart language with gamer/grunge intensity.

sources.title: CARI: McBling
sources.supports: Early-2000s conspicuous glamour, decorative excess and pop-culture luxury motifs.

sources.title: CARI: Gen X Soft Club
sources.supports: Muted urbane futurism distinct from chrome Y2K and flamboyant McBling.

sources.title: CARI: Frutiger Aero
sources.supports: Mid-2000s/early-2010s glossy humanist tech, transparent materials and idealized natural imagery.

sources.title: CARI: Hexatron
sources.supports: 2010s angular science-fiction UI and holographic/terminal imagery.

sources.title: CARI: Cyberbougie
sources.supports: A curator term for sleek startup graphics. Its listed Fluent/glass/neumorphism aliases are rejected as equivalences in our proposal.

sources.title: CARI: Austurbane
sources.supports: Muted refined urban presentation, staged material-rich photography and serif typography.

sources.title: CARI: Blob World
sources.supports: Playful or uncanny rendered forms. Rendering medium alone is not an aesthetic.

sources.title: CARI: Polychrome
sources.supports: Fluid ink/smoke/paint color treatments; classify as imagery/treatment unless they organize the whole visual language.

sources.title: CARI: Corporate Vaporwave
sources.supports: Internet-era recontextualization of 1980s/1990s consumer imagery and nostalgia.

sources.title: CARI: Corporate Memphis
sources.supports: A consumer-aesthetic category; use neutral illustration traits instead of treating the often dismissive nickname as a quality verdict.

sources.title: CARI attribution guidelines
sources.supports: Foundational artist, researcher, name coiner and revival are distinct kinds of attribution.

sources.title: Apple unveils Mac OS X/Aqua
sources.supports: Dated introduction of Aqua with luminous translucent controls; native system provenance rather than a synonym for all Frutiger Aero.

sources.title: Apple unveils iOS 7
sources.supports: Simpler visual structure coexisting with translucency, layers and motion.

sources.title: Apple introduces a new software design
sources.supports: Liquid Glass as Apple's adaptive material across its software platforms.

sources.title: Meet Liquid Glass, WWDC25
sources.supports: Optical/material behavior and content hierarchy; a screenshot cannot verify adaptive behavior or implementation.

sources.title: Material Design 1 introduction
sources.supports: Paper/ink metaphor, spatial organization and motion; Material is not a synonym for fully flat design.

sources.title: Material Design: a look back at its beginning
sources.supports: Creator retrospective on paper prototypes and the 2014 system.

sources.title: Material 3 Expressive research
sources.supports: Expressive shape, color and emphasis in Google's studied product contexts; not universal proof of superiority.

sources.title: Translating design principles to Windows Phone
sources.supports: Metro's typography, content emphasis and layout; official Metro differs from community Frutiger Metro terminology.

sources.title: Fluent 2 materials
sources.supports: Acrylic is translucent; Mica is opaque and tinted; Smoke is a dimming layer. These are not interchangeable glass effects.

sources.title: Characteristics of minimalism in web design
sources.supports: Restraint and hierarchy across several traits; minimal is not simply flat or empty.

sources.title: Neobrutalism: definition and best practices
sources.supports: Bold outlined/shadowed graphic language, contrasted with raw web brutalism.

sources.title: Glassmorphism: definition and best practices
sources.supports: Translucent background-dependent layers and foreground readability; not every shiny photograph is glass UI.

sources.title: Flat design, its problems, and flat 2.0
sources.supports: Fully flat versus selectively dimensional/semi-flat treatment. Avoid copying its imprecise Windows 8 release reference as a launch date.

sources.title: Flat UI elements and clickability signifiers
sources.supports: Study of stronger/weaker signifiers; not a finding that all flat designs are bad.

sources.title: Neumorphism in user interfaces
sources.supports: Paired shading, continuous materials and limitations of effect-driven UI. Author opinion is distinguished from formal comparative studies.

sources.title: Claymorphism in user interfaces
sources.supports: Inflated, rounded surfaces versus low-relief neumorphism; an authored style explanation, not independent usability validation.

sources.title: Claymorphism tutorial
sources.supports: Dated terminology and inner-shadow depth explanation; member-only material beyond the public excerpt was not used.

sources.title: Wim Crouwel
sources.supports: Grid, clarity and typographic structure as enduring professional design principles.

sources.title: Legacies of Swiss Style, part 1
sources.supports: Historical typographic foundations and their diversity; archive objects are not contemporary website samples.

sources.title: Legacies of Swiss Style, part 2: Wolfgang Weingart
sources.supports: Typographic experimentation within and against Swiss modernism; experimental and professional can coexist.

sources.title: Ray Masaki on acid graphics and broken Japanese
sources.supports: Acid graphics' psychedelic/digital lineage and the problem of meaningless decorative language.

sources.title: Seen: MSN and Tamagotchi-inspired digital space
sources.supports: A concrete UI interpretation of soft Y2K/messaging nostalgia, rather than fashion-only moodboards.

sources.title: Nejc Prah's maximalist design
sources.supports: Deliberate visual abundance and expressive typography; print/graphic work, not proof of functioning web UI.

sources.title: Yoffdog's textural maximalism
sources.supports: Hybrid digital/analogue texture and typography in a recent designer practice.

sources.title: Michael Clasen's K1M3R4 cyberpunk publication
sources.supports: Coherent cyberpunk can communicate information rather than rely solely on neon overload.

sources.title: Runblock visual identity
sources.supports: A current identity combining editorial typography and fluid, nostalgic/futurist references; branding rather than UI validation.

sources.title: Bare Earth identity by Blanca Doba
sources.supports: Current gentle botanical/romantic visual direction. Explicitly a fictional-brand exercise, not a production website.

sources.title: Adobe: vintage vaporwave
sources.supports: A specific playful pastel/glitch/consumer-retro interpretation, not a claim about dominance in 2026.

sources.title: Adobe: Austere Romanticism/cottagecore
sources.supports: Botanical, antique, pastoral and academic visual references; exact origins and popularity claims are not treated as settled history.

sources.title: Adobe: vaporwave versus synthwave
sources.supports: Consumer-collage nostalgia versus more cinematic neon science-fiction nostalgia.

sources.title: Rhizome archive
sources.supports: Contemporaneous net-art events/projects as historical references, without treating art as a usable UI benchmark.

sources.title: Dream7, Margaret Penney
sources.supports: 1998–2005 net-art dream/collage/animation work predates today's dreamcore terminology; not proof that the modern labels originated there.

sources.title: Rhizome: Net Aesthetics 2.0
sources.supports: A contemporaneous discussion of art and the changing web in 2006, not the same meaning as glossy Web 2.0 UI.

sources.title: Rosa Menkman: The Glitch Moment(um)
sources.supports: Technical failure and a deliberately used visual language need to be distinguished. Book summary read, not the entire monograph.

sources.title: Brown et al.: nostalgiacores and algorithmic culture
sources.supports: Overlapping hashtags and culturally situated nostalgic imagery; not a standardized UI taxonomy or evidence of 2026 prevalence.

sources.title: Vaporwave Aesthetics: Internet Nostalgia and the Utopian Impulse
sources.supports: Early-2010s genre and ambivalent consumer nostalgia. Repository fetch timed out; unread full text is not claimed.

sources.title: Lu Danqi: Chinese Dreamcore/Weirdcore
sources.supports: Localized meanings and cultural differences; does not certify universal dreamcore/weirdcore visual boundaries.

sources.title: Zombelle and Ultrademon interview
sources.supports: Aquatic internet culture and creators' insistence that context exceeds decorative dolphin imagery.

sources.title: Miss Olivia Louise: solarpunk vision
sources.supports: Craft, Art Nouveau and sustainable technological futures. A cited formative post, not sole invention of the movement.

sources.title: Frutiger Metro community guide
sources.supports: Vector flourishes and music/pop motifs. Broad taxonomy and Windows Metro conflations are treated critically.

sources.title: Frutiger Eco community guide
sources.supports: Eco-optimistic branch of glossy technology/nature imagery; not evidence of sustainability or a solarpunk identity.

sources.title: Aesthetics Wiki: Cybercore
sources.supports: Community vocabulary combining obsolete devices and ethereal/celestial motifs. Direct fetch blocked; precise origins remain uncertain.

sources.title: Aesthetics Wiki: Webcore
sources.supports: Community vocabulary only; direct fetch blocked. Corroborated with creator pages and J01 rather than trusted as a rigid ontology.

sources.title: Aesthetics Wiki: Dreamcore
sources.supports: A discovery lead. Direct fetch failed; main analysis uses J01, J03 and R02 with explicit uncertainty.

sources.title: Aesthetics Wiki: Weirdcore
sources.supports: A discovery lead. Direct fetch failed; do not confuse the label with an artist who uses Weirdcore as a name.

sources.title: Aesthetics Wiki: Kidcore
sources.supports: Childhood toys, primary colors and nostalgic playfulness; full page blocked, boundaries remain community usage.

sources.title: Envato: Y3K and cybersigilism
sources.supports: Current future-facing fashion/graphic terminology. No proof it is a standardized or widely deployed UI language.

sources.title: Hello Kitty and kawaii culture
sources.supports: Character-driven cute visual culture has older Japanese roots and remains active; pastel alone is not kawaii.

sources.title: Sugarangel: creator's old-web/DS-inspired site
sources.supports: Self-described webcore and mixed inspirations. One personal site is not representative of all webcore.

sources.title: Clearglass: webmaster reflections
sources.supports: Variation in old-web practice and criticism of superficial nostalgia shorthand.

sources.title: Linear: calmer interface refresh
sources.supports: Professional restraint can coexist with information density; hierarchy and reducing visual competition are explicit design goals.

sources.title: Linear's interpretation of Liquid Glass
sources.supports: A product-specific reinterpretation of tactile glass, not proof that every glossy website uses Apple's native material.

sources.title: Maria Vasilyeva Portfolio
sources.supports: Observed hero: large serif narrative typography, orderly monochrome surface and layered backdrop. Hero-only inference; no whole-site quality verdict.

sources.title: Odyssée
sources.supports: Observed hero: restrained type with immersive material photography. Glass objects in a photo do not establish glassmorphic controls.

sources.title: twks
sources.supports: Observed hero: immersive organic forms with quiet navigation. Does not prove live 3D, animation or a whole-site aesthetic.

sources.title: RetroCast Now
sources.supports: Observed retro broadcast/weather interface: framed panels, beveled visual elements and period typography; not automatically vaporwave.

sources.title: Maison Kerloïck
sources.supports: Observed mixed-media commerce section: product cutouts, paper-like panel and decorative organic marks. Style/industry are separate.

sources.title: Brutally Human
sources.supports: Observed orderly oversized typography. A name containing brutal does not establish raw web brutalism.

sources.title: Story of Brutalism
sources.supports: Observed architectural subject with large repeated type and a photographic object; architecture theme is not sufficient UI-style evidence.

sources.title: HOVERSTAT.ES current archive
sources.supports: 2025–2026 examples spanning mechanical, typographic, cinematic and experimental presentations. Publisher descriptions are source claims, not independently tested flows.

sources.title: Miranda paper portfolio in Awwwards Hot Right Now
sources.supports: Specific newspaper metaphor and print/editorial layout. No new live inspection of the current site is claimed.

sources.title: Siteinspire typographic category
sources.supports: Actual gallery vocabulary separates style, type, subject and platform; category membership is not section-wide proof.

sources.title: Recent website collection
sources.supports: Discovery of contemporary production websites; no prevalence or quality estimate is derived from gallery inclusion.

sources.title: Awwwards category registry
sources.supports: Available filters mix styles, industries, components and technologies. Search misses can reflect taxonomy/index limits, not absence of an aesthetic.

sources.title: Cybersigilism graphics by Artmoreink
sources.supports: A dated creator-labeled tattoo/streetwear graphic project. Ornamental motifs are not a functioning UI or evidence of UI prevalence.
